correctness.rationale: The bright-space identity is proved directly by Hermitian spectral decomposition and a dissipativity argument, including possible nonnormal Jordan blocks. Hamming Fourier characters give the exact q-ary projector kernel, and a two-by-two projected-monitor Gram rank test fully classifies all q,d and separations. Boundary cases q=2,d=1 and q>=3,d=1 are included. Exact site formulas follow by Gram inversion. The packaged standalone program was run successfully: 23 two-detector distance cases, 394 site comparisons, and direct unequal-rate dissipative propagation. Finite checks are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Prior work supplies the general coherent-transport bright-subspace method and one-absorber binary hypercube result. Full relevant primary sections and targeted research records were compared. The evaluated two-positive-sink all-q spectral rank, distance-independent nonbinary result, binary antipodal exception and arbitrary-vertex Krawtchouk formula were not located in those sources. An unrelated marked coined-search paper does not imply this dissipative theorem. Absolute priority is not asserted and residual stronger-general-theorem risk is recorded.
residual_risks: Potential dominating general algebraic observability/association-scheme theorem, not located by targeted searches; a broader literature search or independent expert could clarify priority.

value.rationale: The number and placement of absorbing sites is a motivated transport-design question: geometric interference leaves a macroscopically large dark subspace. This exact classification for every Hamming alphabet and dimension shows robust detector-placement independence except a sharp binary antipodal obstruction, quantifies the efficiency gain over a single detector, and supplies site-specific probabilities. The q-ary/binary contrast and detector redundancy are structural facts rather than a routine numeric parameter tweak.
